question.:question/problem: Find the particular solution to the differential equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-8(x + 4)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x + 4)$ that satisfies $y(-4 + \frac{\pi}{2})={\pi }^{2}.$ Assume that $0<(x + 4)<\pi .$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We first find the general solution and then apply the given initial condition to find a particular solution.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-8(x + 4)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(x + 4) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(x + 4)+8(x + 4)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x + 4)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)}+8(x + 4) \\ \int \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x + 4)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)}+8(x + 4))\,\text{d}x \\ \int \,\text{d}y & =\int \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x + 4)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)}\,\text{d}x+8\int (x + 4)\,\text{d}x \\ y & =\int \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x + 4)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)}\,\text{d}x+4{(x + 4)}^{2}+{C}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the integral on the right-hand side of this equality, we use a substitution

$$
u=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x + 4)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Then  we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x + 4)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(x + 4)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+{C}_{2} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4))+{C}_{2},\end{aligned}
$$

where we used that $\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)>0.$

Hence,

$$
y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4))+4{(x + 4)}^{2}+C.
$$

where $C={C}_{1}+{C}_{2}$ is an arbitrary constant. 

We now apply the initial condition $y(-4 + \frac{\pi}{2})={\pi }^{2}$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(-4 + \frac{\pi}{2}) & ={\pi }^{2} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{2})+4{\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right)}^{2}+C & ={\pi }^{2} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡1+{\pi }^{2}+C & ={\pi }^{2} \\ C & =0\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the particular solution of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-8(x + 4)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x + 4)$ that satisfies the condition $y(-4 + \frac{\pi}{2})={\pi }^{2}$ is

$$
y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4))+4{(x + 4)}^{2}.
$$

We first find the general solution and then apply the given initial condition to find a particular solution.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 4)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-8(x - 4)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 4) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(x - 4) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 4)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(x - 4)+8(x - 4)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 4) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x - 4)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 4)}+8(x - 4) \\ \int \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x - 4)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 4)}+8(x - 4))\,\text{d}x \\ \int \,\text{d}y & =\int \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x - 4)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 4)}\,\text{d}x+8\int (x - 4)\,\text{d}x \\ y & =\int \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x - 4)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 4)}\,\text{d}x+4{(x - 4)}^{2}+{C}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the integral on the right-hand side of this equality, we use a substitution

$$
u=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 4)\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x - 4)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Then  we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x - 4)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 4)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 4)}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(x - 4)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+{C}_{2} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 4))+{C}_{2},\end{aligned}
$$

where we used that $\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 4)>0.$

Hence,

$$
y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 4))+4{(x - 4)}^{2}+C.
$$

where $C={C}_{1}+{C}_{2}$ is an arbitrary constant. 

We now apply the initial condition $y(\frac{\pi}{2} + 4)={\pi }^{2}$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(\frac{\pi}{2} + 4) & ={\pi }^{2} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{2})+4{\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right)}^{2}+C & ={\pi }^{2} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡1+{\pi }^{2}+C & ={\pi }^{2} \\ C & =0\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the particular solution of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 4)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-8(x - 4)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 4)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x - 4)$ that satisfies the condition $y(\frac{\pi}{2} + 4)={\pi }^{2}$ is

$$
y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x - 4))+4{(x - 4)}^{2}.
$$
